body:
Korea’s GPS is looking for fresh APAC opportunities (Image: GEPS)

A $9 billion South Korean pension fund has launched a search for three fund managers to invest up to $150 million in Asia Pacific real estate.

The Government Employees Pension Service (GEPS), which manages the retirement finances of Korea’s civil servants, plans to commit between $40 million and $50 million to each of two diversified, multi-sector funds and one living sector fund. The details are set out in a request for proposals that GEPS posted on 14 September.

Proposals are due on 29 September, with GEPS, which managed KRW 12.5 trillion ($9.0 billion) in financial assets at the end of 2025, aiming to name the winning managers and sign commitments in early December.

The mandate marks the pension fund’s first commitment to Asia Pacific property in about a decade, and a shift away from the North American and European funds that GEPS backed in its last overseas real estate search in 2024. It also puts GEPS alongside the National Pension Service (NPS) and the Korea Investment Corporation (KIC) in targeting the region’s living sector.

Diversified and Living Strategies

The pension fund will invest with the managers through a domestic vehicle managed by Hyundai Investments, according to the RFP documents. GEPS picked the Hyundai Marine & Fire Insurance unit in April as its local manager for overseas real estate and infrastructure.

GEPS chairman and CEO Kim Dong Keuk (Image: GEPS)

Under the GEPS’ terms, multi-sector funds must target a net internal rate of return of at least 11 percent, and may pursue core, value-add or opportunistic strategies, but single-sector strategies are excluded.

The living sector slot requires a target net IRR of at least 9 percent from residential assets, including senior housing, student accommodation and rental housing. The GEPS ruled out opportunistic strategies for the living sector opportunity, which may be open-ended.

Both mandates exclude mainland China and Hong Kong, while Korean investments are capped at less than 10 percent of the portfolio.

Stakes in operating companies and platforms are limited to 30 percent of each fund and development projects are capped at 50 percent. Management fees may not exceed 1.75 percent of committed capital.

Applicants need at least five years in business, $5 billion in real estate assets under management and $1 billion in Asia Pacific real estate AUM. Proposed funds must reach at least $500 million at final close.

At least one institutional investor with KRW 1 trillion or more in assets must commit to a fund manager’s proposed strategy before GEPS does.

Hyesung Accounting Corp will screen proposals quantitatively with the GEPS planning to notify a shortlist in mid-October, hold presentations in late October and conduct due diligence in mid-November.

GEPS’ last overseas real estate search, in July 2024, targeted global funds with at least 60 percent exposure to North America and Europe. The pension fund allocated $70 million across two managers in that round, according to Korean media.

The Asia Pacific search is the latest step in an expanding overseas alternatives programme.

Last year GEPS shortlisted Bridgepoint, HGGC and Triton for commitments of up to $40 million each to North American and European mid-market buyout funds, according to local news reports. In December the pension fund chose two managers of Europe-focused infrastructure funds for commitments of up to €50 million ($57 million) each.

In its home market, the GEPS in June chose Koramco Asset Management Trust for a Korean blind-pool real estate fund in the pension fund’s first open competition for a domestic property mandate.

Alternatives accounted for KRW 2.2 trillion, or 17.7 percent, of GEPS’ financial assets at the end of 2025, according to the fund’s disclosures. Equities made up 33.8 percent and bonds 27.9 percent, with another 20.6 percent held as a reserve for benefit payments.

GEPS said in June that expanding overseas and alternative investments had helped its medium- and long-term assets return 17.4 percent last year.

Korean Capital Targets APAC Living

The announcement by the GEPS aligns the fund with larger Korean institutions already pursuing Asia Pacific living sector strategies.

In January 2025, Korea’s NPS committed A$700 million to Scape Australia for student accommodation and build-to-rent strategies. The build-to-rent investments are managed by Rent-to-Live Co, a separate company under Scape’s parent, The Living Company.

KIC chief executive Park Il Young said in May 2025 that the sovereign wealth fund was targeting residential and data centre assets in Asian real estate.

On 22 September, South Korean state-backed developer KIND signed an investment agreement with Hyundai Engineering & Construction and Korea Investment Real Asset Management to develop a 45-storey, 260-unit build-to-rent tower in Chatswood in northern Sydney.

Investors expect to deploy $33.2 billion into Asia Pacific residential assets over the next five years, according to Cushman & Wakefield. The firm’s survey found that 85 percent of respondents plan to raise their residential allocations.
